findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts electrical infrastructure including transformers, pull boxes, and meters, but does NOT contain an explicit label designating the Point of Service (POS). The plan shows where proposed underground electric lines enter from Valley View Road (western property line) and connect to electrical pull boxes, but the specific connection point to Austin Energy infrastructure is not labeled as 'Point of Service' or 'POS'. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only a single 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying the POS or primary source. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines on boundaries but no identification of POS. The grouping's regulatory overview (UCM § 1.16.0) requires the POS to be clearly designated, and unless otherwise specified by Austin Energy, the POS must be shown on the required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) and § 1.4.2.6 require that the point of service designation be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans). While Sheet 21 depicts the general electrical routing and infrastructure, the POS is not explicitly labeled or designated. Without clear labeling of the POS location, a reviewer cannot confirm compliance with the requirement to show the 'desired point of electric service' on the plans. This is distinct from merely showing infrastructure; the POS must be explicitly identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors connect or terminate per UCM § 1.3.4.
findings.comment: Point of service (POS) location is not explicitly labeled on any required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows electrical routing and infrastructure but lacks a clear 'Point of Service' designation. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately identify the POS. Add explicit POS labeling to Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing where Austin Energy infrastructure connects to proposed customer infrastructure.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows underground electric line routing with blue lines, conduit connections, and pull box locations. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does NOT show underground electric cabling routing despite being required as a sheet showing 'all utilities.' Sheet 9 displays other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain) with clear line designations but shows only a single transformer pad without any underground electrical lines routing from the source to that pad or to the buildings. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) similarly does NOT show underground electric line routing; it only shows overhead electric (OHE) lines on the western boundary and contains no depiction of the proposed underground electric service lines serving the development. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes a legend entry for 'Underground Electric' but the lines are not actually drawn on the plan view.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations to be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, the landscape plan, and all electrical plans. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) contains detailed electrical routing, the deficiency is that this information must be replicated on the site plan and landscape plan as required plan sheets. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) is identified as showing 'all utilities' but lacks the underground electrical routing information. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) is a required plan sheet per the grouping's regulatory overview but contains no underground electrical infrastructure. Absence of this information on sheets identified as showing utilities constitutes non-compliance, even if the information exists elsewhere in the plan set.
findings.comment: Underground electric cabling routing and conduit locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required 'all utilities' plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add underground electric line routing, conduit paths, and service connections to both sheets showing how power is distributed from the source (Valley View Road connection) to the transformer pads and to building meters.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows two transformer pad locations with explicit labels and symbols. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' near the main entrance (west side, south of Bldg. 2/8 area). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), identified as a required plan sheet showing utilities, does NOT show transformer locations at all. The vision analysis confirmed that Sheet 31 contains no transformer pad symbols, labels, or indications. The landscape plan shows drainage basins and utility line designations (OHE, SD, W) but is completely absent of transformer pad information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires transformer locations to be shown on all required plan sheets: site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. Sheet 21 (electrical plan) and Sheet 9 (site plan) both show transformers, but Sheet 31 (landscape plan) does not. The landscape plan is explicitly listed as a required plan sheet in the grouping's 'Documents to Review' section and the grouping's regulatory overview states that Sheet 31 is required. Omitting transformer locations from the landscape plan violates the requirement to show infrastructure consistently across all required sheets. This is not a redundancy issue; it is a compliance requirement that all required sheets must contain the relevant infrastructure information for complete coordination.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations are not shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite this being a required plan sheet per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Add transformer pad symbols and labels to Sheet 31 matching those shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to ensure complete infrastructure coordination across all utility plan sheets.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electric meter locations clearly labeled as 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors (north walls of Bldgs. 1, 3, 4, 5; south walls of Bldgs. 6, 7; west walls of Bldgs. 2, 8). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not display meter locations - the vision analysis found no meter symbols or labels on this sheet despite it being identified as showing 'all utilities.' Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also does not show meter locations. The meters are confined to Sheet 21 only, and absent from the two required plan sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) that must show utility infrastructure per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 (Point of Service definition) and UCM § 1.4.2.6 (Customer Drawings Specifications) require electric meter locations to be shown on all required plan sheets including the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) contains this information, the requirement specifies that the information must appear on the site plan and landscape plan. Absence of meter locations from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means these required sheets do not adequately document the electrical service infrastructure for review. This prevents verification of meter grouping, spacing, and coordination with other site elements per the meter requirements in UCM § 1.5.2.1(G).
findings.comment: Electric meter locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required plan sheets. Add meter locations to both sheets showing where all electrical meters are positioned on the building exteriors, consistent with the locations shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21).

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows poles and service routing via overhead electric lines on the western boundary (OHE designation) and underground routing throughout the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing overhead electric lines along boundaries (OHE designation) but limited detail on service routing. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines along the southern boundary but does NOT show any specific poles or service drop locations. The vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirmed: 'While an Overhead Electric (OHE) line is shown along the bottom perimeter, specific utility poles are not distinctly labeled, nor are service drops routing power from the main line to the individual buildings.' The landscape plan is deficient in showing poles and service infrastructure details.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires poles or service drops to be shown on all required plan sheets including the landscape plan. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) is explicitly listed as a required plan sheet per the grouping's documents to review and regulatory overview. While Sheet 31 shows overhead electric line designation (OHE), it does not show specific pole locations or service drop routing to buildings. This omission prevents verification of clearances to structures, vegetation conflicts, and proper utility coordination. The grouping's 'Common Violation Patterns' specifically notes 'Incomplete infrastructure across sheets: Electric infrastructure shown on site plan but omitted from landscape plan or electrical plans, violating the requirement to show infrastructure consistently across all required sheets.'
findings.comment: Poles and service drops are not clearly shown on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add pole locations and service drop routing to this sheet to demonstrate coordination with site grading, landscaping, and building placement. Show specific utility pole locations and how overhead or underground service is routed to serve the development.

findings.observation: Examination of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows detailed electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, meters, underground routing, benchmarks, utility notes) but contains NO indication of projected electrical load in any form. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 lists 'Utility Notes' that address contractor requirements and material specifications, but no load information. The 'Key values' section at the beginning of the guide lists building sizes and floor areas but no electrical load figures (kW, kVA, Amps, or service amperage). The sheet's 'Utility Notes' block discusses verification of existing utilities and private water/wastewater specifications but contains no electrical load data. No supplementary documents reviewed (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report) contain electrical load information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires 'projected electrical load' to be shown on plan sheets. This is distinguished from infrastructure location - load information must be documented to allow Austin Energy to verify adequate service capacity and equipment sizing. The absence of any load figures (service amperage, estimated demand, connected load, or design load) on Sheet 21 prevents verification of transformer sizing, conductor capacity, and service adequacy. Without projected load documentation, Austin Energy cannot make an informed determination of line extension requirements, duct bank requirements, vault vs. pedestal service selection, or service point location per UCM § 1.3.12 and § 1.5.2.1.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load is not indicated on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) or any other plan sheet. Add projected electrical service amperage, estimated demand (kW or kVA), or connected load to the electrical design plan. Include load calculations for all buildings and identify the service voltage and amperage for the development.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly designates the service type as UNDERGROUND through explicit labels 'Underground Electric Line' pointing to the routing, blue line styling, and underground pull box locations. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows both existing overhead electric (OHE) on the western boundary AND proposed transformer pad, but the relationship between these and the service type is ambiguous - is the service overhead from the OHE source into an underground distribution on site? Or is there both overhead and underground proposed? The sheet does not explicitly state 'Service Type: Underground' or similar designation. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows OHE (Overhead Electric) lines on the southern boundary but provides no clarity on the overall service type for the development. A reviewer examining Sheets 9 and 31 cannot definitively determine whether the development is served by overhead service, underground service, or a combination without cross-referencing Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires service type (overhead or underground) to be 'clearly designated' on plans. While Sheet 21 makes this clear through labeling and line styling, the requirement is for the designation to appear on all required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and electrical plans). Sheets 9 and 31 do not clearly designate the overall service type. The grouping's 'Common Violation Patterns' specifically lists 'Service type ambiguity: Plans show both overhead and underground elements without clearly designating which service type applies.' A plan reviewer examining the site plan and landscape plan should be able to immediately determine the service type without referencing other sheets.
findings.comment: Service type (overhead or underground) is not clearly designated on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Add a clear note or legend entry on each required plan sheet stating the service type (e.g., 'Proposed Service: Underground Electric Distribution' or similar) to eliminate ambiguity and ensure all required sheets clearly identify whether the development uses overhead, underground, or mixed service type.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electrical easements on the perimeter: '10' P.U.E.' (west), '5' P.U.E.' (north), '15' Easement' and '5' Electric Easement' (east), '5' Elec. Easement' (south). These are dimensioned and labeled around the property boundary. However, the vision analysis noted: 'There are no dimensions or distinct easement boundaries drawn specifically for the internal, proposed underground electrical routing (blue lines) throughout the center of the site.' The grouping's regulatory overview states that UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires showing 'electrical easements' - this includes not only existing/dedicated easements on the plat but also proposed easements for new infrastructure. The internal underground electric line routing (blue lines on Sheet 21) does not have an associated proposed easement boundary shown or dimensioned. The extent of the underground electric easement serving the two transformer pads and internal routing is not delineated or dimensioned on the plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires 'electrical easement locations and extents' to be clearly delineated on plans. The vision analysis and grouping's common violation patterns note 'Electrical easement omissions: Existing or proposed electrical easements not shown or not dimensioned, violating UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i).' While the site plan shows plat-dedicated easements around the perimeter, the proposed easement(s) needed for the new underground electrical infrastructure serving the transformers and internal routing are not explicitly delineated with boundaries or dimensions. An easement width is not specified for the proposed underground electric distribution serving the development.
findings.comment: Proposed electrical easement locations and extents for the new underground electric distribution are not clearly delineated or dimensioned on the electrical design plan. Add easement boundaries and dimensions showing the width and extent of the easement(s) required to accommodate the proposed underground electric routing, transformers, and infrastructure within the site. Verify easement widths meet Austin Energy requirements for maintenance and future replacement.

findings.observation: Review of the site plan sheets (1-39) and supplementary documents reveals NO One-Line Diagram of an electrical riser included in the plan set. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows site layout, transformers, and routing but does not contain a one-line diagram. The README documentation lists all 39 sheets of the primary site plan, with Sheet 21 described as showing 'Layout of preliminary electrical design, routing, transformers, and meters' - this describes a site plan view, not a riser one-line diagram. No other electrical schematic or one-line diagram is mentioned in the sheet index. The supplementary documents (Engineer's Summary Letter, Master Comment Report, etc.) do not reference a one-line diagram. The grouping's regulatory overview explicitly lists 'Missing One-Line Diagram: Plan set does not include One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser required by Table 1.4.3.B' as a common violation pattern.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B (Customer Drawings Specifications) explicitly requires 'One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser' as a mandatory component of the plan set. This is not optional and is a separate submittal from the site plan sheets. The one-line diagram must show the electrical service configuration, including service entrance, main distribution panel, branch circuits, protective devices, and load breakdown per building or service point. The absence of this document from the plan set is a clear violation of the requirement. The grouping's regulatory overview notes this is a required plan sheet per Table 1.4.3.B.
findings.comment: One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser is not included in the plan set. Provide a complete one-line diagram showing the electrical service configuration including main service entrance, distribution panel(s), protective devices, branch circuits, and load distribution per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. The diagram must clearly show how the service from Austin Energy connects to the customer's electrical system and distributes power throughout the development.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows two electrical transformer pads, which may indicate two service points, but the vision analysis and detailed examination do not reveal explicit documentation of service voltage or whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved. The plan shows: 'Two proposed transformers shown, and both are explicitly designated as pad-mounted. One is located on the western side of the property...The second is located on the eastern side of the property.' The question is whether these two transformers serve different buildings with different voltages (which would violate the one-voltage rule) or whether they are both serving the same development at the same voltage (which would be acceptable step-down transformers). The blocks.md for Sheet 21 does not specify the voltage(s) for each transformer. No documentation from Austin Energy (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement) was provided that would confirm whether exceptions to the one-POS/one-voltage rule have been approved.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(5) allows 'only one point of service and one service voltage' unless exceptions are 'approved by Austin Energy Design.' The presence of two transformers on the plan is not inherently a violation if they are both part of a single service point and serve the same voltage. However, without explicit documentation of the service voltage and Austin Energy approval for the transformer configuration, it cannot be verified whether the requirement is met. The grouping's regulatory overview states: 'Several infrastructure requirements cannot be determined from site plan review alone and require formal determination by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process' and specifically lists 'Vaults and pedestals: Service type selection is made during AE Design coordination and documented in Letter of Agreement or ESPA approval.' Similarly, the one-POS/one-voltage requirement requires Austin Energy confirmation. This item cannot be marked pass without evidence of AE approval, nor can it be marked fail without evidence of AE non-compliance.
findings.comment: Clarification needed regarding the two transformer pads shown on Sheet 21 and whether they represent separate services with different voltages. Provide Austin Energy documentation (ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement) confirming whether the two transformers are part of a single point of service at one voltage, or whether exceptions to UCM § 1.16.0(5) have been approved for multiple service points or voltages. If the transformers are step-down stages of a single service, add labeling to Sheet 21 clarifying the service configuration and voltage(s).
